page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU runs at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and is equipped with 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a local 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are present.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 25%. Geekbench text processing also demonstrates strong performance. However, multi-core execution falls into the average range, as seen in the stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. Memory bandwidth presents a notable tradeoff, with read-only operations for both small and large blocks scoring in the bottom 25%, while large block write bandwidth remains average. Cryptographic and compression workloads, such as gzip compression and Passmark CPU encryption, perform at average levels, whereas database operations and Redis SET operations show weaker performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4ads_v6 offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads that require a mix of compute, memory, and fast local temporary storage without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The inclusion of a local NVMe SSD provides efficient scratch space. This server is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, text processing, lightweight single-threaded applications, and general-purpose development environments. It is less optimal for memory-bandwidth-intensive applications, heavy database operations, or large-scale multi-threaded compilation tasks.
